title: Usage wire protector and ingest inspection pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose:
This ticket creates a lightweight "wire protector" layer in front of the existing usage event intake to detect and quarantine structurally anomalous payloads early, provide richer failure diagnostics to the Console, and emit sampled artifacts for offline schema evolution analysis. The goal is to reduce noisy downstream failures (parsers, enrichers, evals) and to give product and SRE teams actionable telemetry when producers break contract.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Deploy a non-blocking inspection proxy that tags events as PASS / QUARANTINE / REJECT with reason codes and preserves original payload for sampled events.
- QUARANTINE flows should be automatically routed to a lightweight S3 staging bucket + inspect job for faster triage; REJECTed events should return a 4xx with a clear error code for known contract violations.
- Surface aggregated quarantine metrics in Console: rate by reason, top producer IDs, and time-to-resolution.
- End-to-end latency impact < 4ms P50 on the fast path; fast-path must remain non-blocking for known-good producers.
- Provide a runbook and automated alerting for quarantine surge (thresholds: 0.5% of traffic or >50 qps sustained).

Technical approach:
1) Implement a thin HTTP proxy written in Rust (existing ingress stack components). The proxy will perform schema-surface checks (required keys, message_size, timestamp monotonicity) and lightweight heuristics (unexpected enum values, base64/JSON encoding errors). The checks are intentionally conservative to avoid false positives.
2) Protocol: examine Content-Type and X-Producer-Version headers. Use a small, cached set of typed validators (schema fingerprints) keyed by producer and version. If no validator exists, mark as UNSTAMPED and sample for offline analysis rather than rejecting.
3) Quarantine handling: QUARANTINEed events are stored to a compressed, partitioned S3 prefix with metadata (producer, shard, reason, received_at). A scheduled job (ingest-inspector) will run targeted validations and produce a summary artifact per hour.
4) Rejection policy: only apply deterministic rejections (malformed JSON, missing top-level envelope, signature/tamper check failures). All other deviations go to QUARANTINE.
5) Observability: emit structured telemetry to the internal telemetry topic: decision, latency_ms, validator_key, sampling_id. Add tracing hooks to correlate producer call ids to quarantine artifacts.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Full strict validation at the edge (rejected many producers) vs conservative quarantine-first approach. Chosen quarantine-first to avoid customer-visible regressions.
- Inline heavy schema validation (more CPU) vs offload to an async inspector. Chosen hybrid: fast checks inline + sampling to async workers for expensive validations.
- Language choice: Rust for low-latency and safety. We evaluated Go but preferred zero-cost abstractions for parsing and fewer GC spikes.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable for 5% of traffic of non-critical producers (start with internal dashboards, dev teams). Monitor key metrics for 48h.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback on high-latency or quarantine surge.
- Post-rollout: run a 7-day sampling job to aggregate schema diffs and present to product/SDK owners.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Latency: P50 < 4ms, P95 < 12ms for fast-path PASS.
- Correctness: false-positive rate for quarantine < 0.05% (measured against a gold sample set).
- Coverage: at least 80% of long-tail producer versions must be marked UNSTAMPED and get sampled for analysis within 72 hours.
